title: LandscapeResponse
description:
What a landscape query returns (BRIEF-2.2-b): scalar terms, exact deltas where the provider is decomposable, optional gradients, per-position tracks, and per-term uncertainty with provenance.

DESIGN NOTE ON GRADIENTS. The design space is discrete - a codon is a categorical choice among synonyms - so a gradient only exists with respect to a continuous relaxation. DNA Design Suite fixes that relaxation once, here: the parameterization is a per-position simplex over the synonymous set (`relaxed_codon_logits`), and a gradient is d(term)/d(logit). Any other reading of `gradient` is rejected at review. For decomposable terms, exact deltas are strictly more useful than gradients, since they are the true finite change rather than a linearization; see ADR-0002.

DESIGN NOTE ON PARTIAL RESULTS. `status: partial` is a first-class outcome, not an error. A provider that misses its latency budget returns what it has. The search engine treats absent terms as `unknown`, which the NSGA-III constraint-domination rule handles by deferring the candidate rather than by imputing a value - imputing would silently bias the front.

terms.description: Scalar value per requested term. A term absent from this map when status=partial means 'not computed', which is semantically distinct from a null value.

reference_range.description: [p05, p95] of this term across the host's native highly-expressed CDS set. Gives the decision-support layer a scale for 'is this value unusual' without hard-coding units, and gives hypervolume a principled reference point.

capability.description: Highest capability this provider offers for this term. The engine uses it to plan tier 2.

objective_vector.description: The scalarization-free objective vector handed to NSGA-III, with its ordering stated explicitly. Never infer the order from `terms` key iteration.

per_position.description: Per-codon diagnostic tracks, length == codon_count. These are what the rationale tagger in cf-decision turns into user-facing explanations.

confidence.description: Per-position confidence in [0,1], produced by the Mondrian-conformal procedure in ADR-0005. Null where the method does not support per-position calibration.

deltas.description: Exact change in each decomposable term for each synonymous alternative. Populated only for a delta_table target. Missing terms in an entry mean the provider is L0 for that term.

exact.description: True when deltas are computed in closed form; false when they are finite-difference or surrogate estimates. The repair operator requires exact=true to guarantee its minimality property.

parameterization.description: Fixed by contract. shape = [codon_count, max_synonyms]; entries beyond a position's synonym count are null.

temperature.description: Softmax temperature of the relaxation. Reported because the gradient scale is meaningless without it.

violations.description: Hard-constraint violations detected during scoring. Reported here as well as by cf-constraints so that an out-of-core provider (e.g. a structure engine that finds a hairpin over the RBS) can raise one.

full_rescores.description: Terms whose value came from rescoring the mutated sequence in full because the provider could not answer a delta query. Reported because it is the only observable that distinguishes per-term degradation from per-query degradation: a composition that abandoned the exact-delta path for every term because one term lacked it returns identical numbers and differs only here. Zero on a full-sequence query, where there is no delta path to abandon.

rebases.description: Providers pinned to a base sequence during this query. A coordinate-ascent sweep should rebase once per (base, term) and then issue many delta queries against it; a count that tracks the number of moves means the O(L) pin is being paid per move, which costs the exact-delta path its whole advantage. See DEP-LAND-003.
